newsitem.title: UK: British taxman threatens German soccer stars.
newsitem.headline: British taxman threatens German soccer stars.

text.p: Britain may get the last laugh after Germany's European soccer championship victory over England this summer, with tax officials claiming penalties of up to 21,000 pounds ($33,000) for each player, the Times newspaper reported on Monday.
It said Britain's Inland Revenue was checking to see whether the German players, along with some Czech and French players, had paid enough tax on their appearance money.
Players such as Juergen Klinsmann, Oliver Bierhof and Christian Ziege, who earned 85,000 pounds ($136,000) each from the tournament, topped the list, according to the Times.

Withholding tax of 25 percent is routinely levied on foreign athletes such as golf and tennis players competing in Britain. But the newspaper said the soccer players were paid directly by the associations and the tax was not taken out.
